text: I met this restaurant this summer and I just love it! They serve foods from different countries with a especial flavour made by the Chef. The Mac'n cheese is really good, and is a place to feel a little of the culture of the country that come the food. The attendance is very good and welcoming. And the place are beautiful that show care with details.
name: Rigodon

text: Had an amazing meal at El Viajero Del Merkao. Saw the trip advisor and Yelp reviews were very good so tried it and was extremely impressed. Food was flawless, wine was also very good and super inexpensive. The owner was extremely nice and did a good job of recommending great dishes. We loved the octopus and the croquettes, but honestly everything we had was good.
name: El Viajero Del Merkao

text: Four of us enjoyed a very pleasant meal here last Saturday evening. We had a variety of pasta meals and all greatly enjoyed the choice they had made. The wine list was perfectly reasonable and satisfied our needs. HOWEVER when the bill came we very very disappointed and somewhat irritated that our pre dinner drinks (Four gin and Tonics) cost €50!! Insult had been added since I had asked for a sherry and they had none to offer. We suggest they perhaps review their pricing and their choice of stock.
name: La Tarantella

text: Jaipur Purple always serves very good food. Last night I had my 2 benchmark dishes so I could compare it with other Indian restaurants . My starter was chicken pakora which was lovely and crispy as it should be but often is not in other restaurants. My guests had Tandoori mushrooms and vegetable cutlets which were both delicious too. For my main course I Had Chicken Phal which is a hotter version of vindaloo. it was delicious and not too hot for me. My companions had a chicken Jalfrezi and Chicken Tikka Masala which I tasted and were both very good too with quality ingredients and lots of flavour. We shared a Garlic Naan bread and had 3 different rice dishes all washed down with lots of chilled white wine. In my opinion this is a better Indian than others I have tried here on the coast. The indoor setting may make it less attractive to some diners but for me it's all about the food. Service is very friendly and efficient and we received a complimentary drink with our bill. I recommend a visit to Jaipur Purple.
name: Jaipur Purple

text: Today i went with my mom and dog to " La Piká " coming for several years to Mojacar, this visit was one of my best in a long time. People look for a nice solution between our dog and not disturbing other people without dogs. He was very welcome. The menu is suprising and very different from other restaurants. The white " housewine " Verdejo was Wonderfull and all dishes were perfect. The service was great and felt very familiar. I can recommend this place to everybody!! Top of the bill, see you soon again... very soon and yes the home made vanilla icecream ..... thanks La Piká !!! Good job !!!
name: La Pika

text: This restaurant can be found at the far end of San Jose's harbour, quite some distance from where it shows up on TripAdvisor and Google Maps. But is it worth seeking out? In my view, probably not. Don't get me wrong, it's a very smart place with good views and friendly service. But the food was a bit of a disappointment. I'm always reluctant to order paella in Spain. That may sound odd but in my experience it's a dish that too often is reheated rather than freshly made. But I thought I'd give it a go here as they seemed to specialise in rice dishes and I thought their offering may be a cut above the average. Unfortunately it wasn't. It was ok but no better than that. When a paella arrives within 20 minutes of ordering it you know that the chef has taken some shortcuts. I wouldn't recommend it.
name: 4 Nudos

text: Contemporary decor with great Med views from its terrace. Service starts with a good welcome from professional waiters. Food is modern 'gourmet' international style, not typically Spanish. Neither is it fusion, overall good well presented with well balanced flavours...except the great failure of drowning a small steak with a horrible sweet mustard sauce concoction. Returning the dish almost untouched to the waiter resulted in nothing more than a 'sorry' . All 4 diners had scraped the sickly slime off the meat but ate some of it anyway. Failing to offer a replacement was a double failing removing this place from our list of dining venues. Lighting is unfortunately the typical Spanish bar pure white blinding LED light which ruins the atmosphere the decorator tried to create. Tapas lunch menu is good.
name: Escorpio Restaurante

text: Unfortunately the road is being developed outside this restaurant so it was rather dusty and noisy but of course this is no fault of the restaurant. Instead of sitting outside in the sunshine we decided to have our lunch inside where the decor was decidedly Mexican so it was nice and bright. Service was very good and the food excellent and very well priced.
name: Restaurante Mexicano Riviera Maya

text: This restaurant is perfect if you want three courses at a very low price. There are many restaurants like this on the Playa. However if you just are looking for a high quality main course meal without starter and desert, similar to what is available in a small number of quality restaurants on the Playa, such as La Pika, then this is probably not the place for you. We were amazed how they could afford to charge such low prices for three courses? Especially as tipping is not common practice by locals in Spain. On the negative side, Food providence was certainly not organic. The vegetables were of poor quality and overcooked. The potato fries covered in olive oil and not palatable. This is very much a restaurant catering for those on a tight budget. The place was busy and the facilities were clean. The staff were friendly and helpful.
name: Torre Bahia

text: This beautiful restaurant in the Old Town in Marbella served the most amazing food. The scallops & veal carpacio style were had for starters & were mouthwatering. For mains we had monkfish & prawn with chorizo & broad bean risotto, tortello stuffed with confit duck & foie gras sauce & linguini in a lemon butter sauce with crab legs & a touch of chilli. Totally sublime. We will definitely be back on our next visit.
name: Il Tartufo

text: I ordered the daily deal menu because I was walking past and starving. Food tasted bland but edible. The smell of burnt dirty cooking oil gradually got worse until I had to leave before finishing. The smell was stuck to my clothes. Got home and was sick all night. This was the only thing I'd eaten all day so it was definitely this food. Avoid this restaurant.
name: Promo China

text: The Spanish dispute the English claim to the be the 'inventors' of fried fish. Freiduria can be found all over Andalusia. This one served several different types of bite-sized batter-coated fried fish. It is sold by 250 gram portions. You can pick up a 'Variada' for about 5 euros- this gets you a bit of everthing. I'd recommend that you ask them to do it without Shrimps ('sin Gambas')- as they are not deveined- no doubt Spanish stomachs are a bit more used to seafood- those of us with more delicate Anglo-Saxon digestive systems need to be a bit more careful. You'll have to order in Spanish- no English spoken- and the Freiduria itself was choc full of locals when we went. It was also notable that the local tapas bars were collect large orders of fried fish- presumably to sell on that night. There's a little 'greasy spoon' type dining area- but, because the fish is served in cones you can eat it as you wander the atmospheric streets of Triana. Highly recommended.
name: Freiduria Reina Victoria

text: I visited on 19th May 2019 to celebrate a special birthday. We had a fabulous time there, food excellent, service second to none. On arrival as we were asked on booking lunch if it was a special occasion we were greeted with champagne and once the meal was over they brought out a birthday cake which tasted yummy. All in all a fantastic celebration of my birthday and I would like to thank Shea and all his wonderful staff for their attention to detail. Shea himself comes to visit all the tables once his duties of cooking in the kitchen is done....so lovely to see the Chef chatting to his customers.... I can highly recommend this restaurant to anybody wanting to enjoy a wonderful ambience with food that we can't fault. A set three course menu for Sunday lunch with an excellent choice of meats and fish. Well worth a visit if you come to Mojacar. We can't wait to visit again.
name: Restaurante La Parata

text: I hesitated before booking for my wife's birthday with a group of friends and their kids as some told me they didn't like the experience last summer, but took the advice of my hotel's concierge and booked. They have three dining areas, the garden which is absolutely charming, the main restaurant inside which is well furnished and decorated, and an adjacent terrace where we were seated as it was a large group. The service was excellent, excellent wine selection and a great creative menu. Highly recommended for dinner or just drinks, i would go again next time in Banus and would ask for a garden table...
name: Breathe

text: Well that was underwhelming !! Starter was Brochette on a slate that resulted in the tomato etc falling on the table cloth!!? I ordered a main of paste with green pesto and pine nuts... 4!!.... Nuts!!!!.... Glass of wine €3.50!! eee... Why... It's average wine ... €2.20 max.... Waiters do not have tables allocated, had 3 different waters ask me if I wanted to order... Why... !!! Live in the Pueblo.. This is my second and LAST visit to La Pala D'Oro .... Want to waste money, ... in my opinion come here. Way-over priced for what you get.... Cordado coffee ok but €2 !!! Waiters indifferent ... Not trained, lack experience, young .
name: La Pala d Oro

text: We had a long day and wanted a hearty dinner. This place had good reviews on yelp. Decided to eat here. Ambience was what drew us in at first- very cozy yet stylish and grand. Staff was a bit slow but that's how people eat meals in spain No rush .... We were given an assortment of local breads and breadsticks while we waited for our meal. The food eventually arrived- so tasty and delicious!!!! Fresh pasta and fresh ingredients. Both items we ordered were prepared perfectly and were a very satisfying portion! Had a very delicious dinner so much so that we had no room for dessert A nice spot for a meal while visiting Marbella.
name: Da Bruno A Casa

text: We visited this place twice, the first time I ordered scampi which was on the menu and it came out as prawns in batter!!!! So don't get the scampi, if you want it they give you prawns!! The second time I had pizza, it was ok, but it was quite small! But the staff are friendly enough and they were very busy! I was just a little dissapointed with my choices! Apparently the steak is lovely!!
name: Trattoria Italiana

text: Went to restaurant with my partner & family. The tasting menus have something for everyone. They advised and swapped a few things when they found out one of our party was pregnant. Top class service nothing was too much trouble & when one of our party had too leave as feeling ill they knocked €10 off the cost of his food. Great dinning with great views in summer. Highly recommended will definitely visit again.
name: Escorpio Restaurante

text: One of the few restaurants open in January (2015) when we visited the site of the Roman city of Baelo Claudia, and annoyingly difficult to find (you can see it from inside the site, but to get to it you need to go back to Bolonia and follow the track to the beach). Right on the beach, and a tad expensive no doubt in view of its situation, but good quality fish dishes (swordfish and lemon fish dishes for around 12 Euros each), good service, and a choice of eating outside or indoors.
name: Bar Restaurante Otero

text: We called here whilst we were having a long walk on the promenade on our last day, firstly we stopped for a mid morning drink, but were impressed by the friendliness of the staff and what was on offer on the menu, so we decided to return after our walk was completed and treat ourselves to lunch, All day breakfast for 6 euro's something and the menu del dia, 3 courses for 10 euro, what more could you want. Lovely location to either have a drink or a meal, very clean and well presented with very friendly staff who made you feel welcome, great food and equally good value, highly recommended, well worth a visit.
name: Blue Palm

text: A lovely little restaurant hidden away in Albox. The food is excellent quality at a very reasonable price, the set menu having lots of choices and includes a carafe of wine. The decor is lovely and the tables are dressed well - it's nice to find somewhere with proper tablecloths and napkins! And the butter doesn't come in plastic cartons either! We've been a few times now, and the owner kindly kept our sunglasses we left a few months ago. It's a place for for special occasions, there's always someone celebrating something! We will be back.
name: La Cena

text: I had heard good comments about La Estancia so having not tried this restaurant it was the perfect excuse. The ambiance is very warm, ideally located with great sea views. We ordered steak from the menu which was absolutely divine. Perfectly cooked as per our request. Service is excellent, hardly any waiting time to be served. We also had a desert which again was fantastic. Reasonably priced this restaurant definitely gives value for money and I would highly recommend.
name: La Estancia

text: We did not have a bad dinner, but most definitely not to be repeated. Staff was uninterested, we were a family having an early dinner, and probably more interested in the later 'party' side of the evening. Too expensive for the food served. I guess you pay for location, but not worth it to us. Way better quality to be found in the area.
name: La Sala

text: We stumbled across this fine restaurant on our walk through the Marina area of Benalmádena. Both in the mood for a juicy steak this place did not disappoint. I ordered the 10oz ribeye and my partner ordered the 8oz filet. The quality of the food was excellent. The price was inline with what we would expect to pay at a restaurant like this so another win! From the first moment we sat down the staff were very pleasant and attentive. There were a good few customers sat down at 8pm when we arrived. Usually a good sign as to the quality of the place. We would both happily return for dinner next time we are here on holiday. Thanks from two satisfied customers.
name: The Steakhouse

text: We booked this restaurant from Trip Adviser recommendation. A lovely restaurant, typically family owned. At first we were very surprised that the menu was only available in Spanish (fortunately I was able to translate) being in such close proximity to Larios Street. We were also surprised that there was no potato option either so a bit confused. However when it came to ordering the waiters could not have been more helpful, They provided some home style garlic bread for my fussy husband for a starter and our sharing plate of buffalo mozarella was gorgeous. They also made some home cut french fries for my husband as a one off. The steak was absolutely divine as was the pasta dish. Not a huge choice of desserts but the tiramisu was really nice. So what started out as a bit of a "who chose this restaurant" to a "really enjoyed this restaurant". So pleasantly surprised.
name: Osteria Angelino dal 1899 Malaga

text: I booked a VIP bed on a busy Saturday. On our arrival we were escorted to our sunbed which was in a good position and our host for the day Horatio greeted us. We were well looked after the whole day with nothing being too much trouble. The atmosphere and music is brilliant. Drinks are expensive but food is of a very high standard and very reasonable. Overall is was quite an expensive day paying for 5 adults but we all thoroughly enjoyed ourselves so it was well worth it.
name: Ocean Club Marbella

text: Friendly local restaurant. I have visited many times with my family and friends. I have never sat inside, it does not seem that great inside actually, so the five stars are for enjoying an "al fresco" meal. No Michelin stars will be awarded here, but for a great local meal, good service and a fantastic ambiance this is the place, oh yeah those Pizzas too, they are so good, should you really risk ordering anything else?
name: El Parador

text: Popped in from my hotel which was pretty much next door after resisting the sharp sweet odours of sour ,garlic and lemon . I got straight to brass tacks and got a bottle of Faustino VII in ( Blanco ) . The noodles would have been enough and they didn't skip on the Gambas . Loads to choose from here and it was a surprise to find I recognised little on the menu had it not been for the well defined breakdown as listed . I found it a little hurried but I guess I was solo . The waiters were on a learning curve but the Manageress was impeccable . Pious and very enjoyable none the less .
name: Asian Fusion Bing Thai Restaurant

text: This restaurant is such fun, and has such a happy ambiance. The tapas menu is great for sharing with a group of friends. A family run restaurant, the staff are friendly and helpful. The food is incredibly reasonably priced, and freshly cooked, and tastes great. We always call it the garage. Because it does look as if the rear room was once a garage, which has now been painted white with pots of geraniums hanging off the walls. I would recommend: the stuffed peppers - so moreish, the aubergines with treacle - yummy, gambas pil pil - cheapest around, large grilled prawns with garlic - gorgeous. The dishes of fried and grilled fish to share a just great. Be warned, this restaurant is incredibly popular with the local Spanish. If you go after 9pm you will have to wait for a table. Trust me, it'll be worth it.
name: Las Gitanillas

text: This unassuming Spanish tapas style restaurant provided us with a real surprise. The quality and presentation of the food was excellent and at only 2.50 euro per dish , this is the bargain of the century ! If this place was in Puerto Banus you would pay at least 10 euro a dish. Can't recommend it highly enough, if you are in Estepona , definitely go to El Toque.
name: El Toque

text: We saw that this place was advertising a flamenco show and booked it right away. The show was not the best since it's a group of 3 young people trying to get started, but it was entertaining. The owner was on site and made our stay very enjoyable. The food was amazing and the service was very good. We would definitely come eat here again.
name: El Quinque

text: El Rincon Del Zahori sits high above the Plaza Nueva so you have a view of the Mojacar Pueblo and the beach and sorrounding area. The foot is mostly pastas, pizzas, seafood and salads - which are all very good. A favorite for my 11 year old son is the Pasta Carbonera. My favorite is a Tinto de Verano and a Seafood Platter.
name: Rincon Del Zahori

text: Eight of us eating, menu extensive. Very large portions, fresh & really tasty. Abbey the waitress really friendly & helpful. Went out to eat at 10pm & was not rushed. Had vegetarian in our group & chef was more than happy to accommodate meat meals for what he was happy to eat. Price was €190, that included drinks, some starters and main courses. The meals we had ranged from fajitas, mixed grill, burritos, T-bone steaks & chicken. Everyone was satisfied & bulging!
name: Tex Mex Gringo s

text: We ate here two years ago and last year also. The menu was largely local and food cooked with care. The menu now is Asian fusion with, seemingly, lots of Korean influence....why? We ordered three dishes to share, the first a prawn dish, which was heavily salted, the second a fried duck croquet...quite mushy with little taste and then a ham on toast that was so salty it was inedible. Give the restaurant it's due, the fact we left two courses was noticed and we weren't charged, and their attitude was very regretful we hadn't enjoyed eating there. A great shame but the change, in our view, is for the worst.
name: 4 Estaciones Vejer

text: We had the most amazing meal here. It was €32 between 2 of us and you got a starter salad, a giant veal steak with potatoes, chips and peppers ( you got a big gas skillet plate to cook the veal to your liking) the most creamy and delicate peppercorn sauce, plus a bottle of wine. The quality of meat was amazing it just melted in your mouth, the potatoes and peppers were so tasty. We were so full but couldn't stop dipping until the peppercorn sauce. We will definitely be returning next year!!!
name: Frutos Del Mar

text: booked online a ticket for flamenco show. 20 euros include a show and complementary drink. they charge 5 euros in advance and you pay the rest at the restaurant. the show was very nice , but it started 20 minutes late and lasted around 1h15min with a pause. the show itself consisted of two parts, in between 2 dancers change dresses. there were 4 people - guitar player, singer and dancing couple. all in all very nice experience. you can park nearby, but everything was busy on a summer evening , had to use underground parking 10 minutes away by foot.
name: Restaurante Tipi Tapa

text: We ate here as at first, we got from CLC a Privilege card to use on our resort but also at certain restaurants around Fuengirola. So, we were given a 10% discount on the bill which wasn't expensive anyway. The choice was amazing and was difficult to decide but the quality of the service and food was excellent. It's situated very close to the beach on the main road. We will be back in December.
name: Asian Fusion Bing Thai Restaurant

text: Been here couple of times now and enjoyed all the food. The tip I would give when ordering food is to ask for little more spice. I love Thai food but this tends to be milder than what we are used to so people of the same mind would be slightly disappointed. But the food is of a high standard and will be visiting again I am sure.
name: Top Thai Restaurant

text: Near the far end of Sabinillas opposite the kids play park and fitness area. This is one you MUST try out. Excellent service - first class Tapas with generous portions. Superb prices, you will really get a good value meal here in a nice venue where the staff really care and go the extra mile. Eat in or out. Highly recommended !
name: La Casita

text: Best food we ate in a long time! We spent a week in Fuengirola and we ate here three times, each time was as good as the first. Really friendly and professional staff.The food was so tasty and fresh.My husband had the mixed grill, I had lamb madras twice and lamb Vindaloo and I really have to say they were the tastiest, most perfectly spiced dishes I have had in any Indian restaurant.We also had three of our young daughters with us and they loved it. I'm only sorry they d'ont have a restaurant in southern Ireland!!!Would definitely recommend a visit.
name: Masala Korma

text: We came here whilst on holiday in la cala de mijas for my birthday; my boyfriend booked it as a surprise. We were welcomed into the restaurant and seated outside with great views overlooking the lake and surrounding apartments. We had a choice of 2 taster menus or a la carte- we opted for the 5 course classic taster menu with wine pairings. When each course arrived the sommelier described the paired wine and the dish was also explained; and any questions we had about the dishes were answered with knowledge. Each course was faultless (especially the octopus) considering we've eaten at Michelin establishments before, plus being poured extra wine and offered more bread with each course was a bonus. By the end of the 5 courses we were stuffed, plus the restaurant providing a proposal plate and champagne for my boyfriend to propose was the perfect ending. We want to say an extra thank you to the sommelier and Andrea (we think it was her second day working there) for looking after us the whole evening, and nothing was too much. We will definitely be back next time we're in the south of spain!
name: Restaurante El lago

text: Called in at 18.00 place was empty, chose the days special of steak with jacket potato and vegetables. Waiter was very pleasant and we had a drink whilst waiting.The place soon filled up and when the meal arrived it didn't dissapoint. Really well presented and cooked.Waiter very good and although not over attentive was on hand if required. Complimentary cream liqueurs when settling the bill. Definitely going back.
name: Las Rias

text: Went here for my Birthday after doing my research. The ambience and waiting staff score high. But the food was unremarkable. The salad on the side order plates was limp and pathetic. Three things we ordered werent available- the wine we chose, the thai fish cakes and the green tea icecream. Chocolate icecream dosent really add anything to a thai meal. I expected a lot better.
name: Naga

text: We really enjoyed our dinner at Palacio de Gallego. It's a lovely place with tables spread out in the courtyard of an old palace on a back street near the cathedral. It's a very romantic setting with the tables nicely spaced so you don't feel like you're squashed up against your neighbour. And the food - with meat & seafood coming straight off the barbeque - is just great. We started with some fried aubergines with honey and a goat's cheese salad. The former were superb - really light unlike some soggy, greasy versions of the same dish served elsewhere. Both starters were pretty large and in hindsight we could easily have shared one. For mains we had the octopus and the tuna. Absolutely amazing. Just delicious. The tuna was super rare so we had to ask them to pop it back on the flames for a few seconds which they were happy to do. When it returned it was perfect. The bill came in at around €70 including two small beers and two glasses of house wine so it's far from cheap by Andalusian standards. But it's well worth it. Just go. You won't regret it.
name: Palacio De Gallego

text: Thanks to Haley and everyone at Lews yesterday, Sunday 10th April, for a lovely roast lunch for me and my mum, had the beef and chicken which were both so good and followed by cherry pie and homemade apple crumble which were both delicious. Then watched all there football as well for a perfect Sunday afternoon!! Thank you for everything and see you soon.
name: Lews Restaurant Bar

text: Dinner on NYE not a good idea at the best of times as restaurants seem unable to cope and this was no exceptin food was very mediocre €65 per head including wine and cava but quite honestly we'd rather have eaten at home!!! Not expensive by English standards but quite a lot for the Spanish pocket wouldn't return New Year or not!
name: Restaurante Sevillano

text: Came here with my family, 6 adults ranging from 28 to 73 years old and 1 toddler ages 2.5, we sat outside and the view was nice but not the best there is to be had in the area I'm sure but you might not get the same quality of food and service elsewhere... Every single member of our party all thoroughly enjoyed our food (even my little boy who is getting very fussy ate all of his spag bol!) and the service was excellent, even when my son knocked over a full glass of juice, the waiter was brilliant. I definitely recommend this place!
name: Peccati Di Gola

text: Lovely and excellent home made vegan food. Many options. I eat here every day at lunch and I take food with me for the evening. I had the chickpea soup, the zuchini tomato dish, broccoli pasta, the famous tortilla and yesterday at Valentine's day, they had a lovely vegan cake. The lady is very friendly and welcoming. All very tasty, filling and inexpensive food. My non-vegan friend like it also very much. Go there you all, if you are in Cadiz! The Mercado is a special experience. Don't miss La Veganesa!
name: La Veganesa

text: We were welcomed by a staff member and went up in the lift to the terrace. The view was superb. We were the first guests to arrive. The waiter service was excellent. The menu was extensive and catered well for our mixed group, with a good choice of seafood, vegetarian and meat. The pork tomahawk was quite spectacular. The wine menu was good. We thoroughly enjoyed our meal. We will return when next in Seville and would happily recommend to family and friends.
name: Betis 7 Triana Experience

text: The area seemed buzzing so we thought we'd try this place. Being our first time in spain we decided to try the national dish 'Paella'. We ordered the fish paella for the family. What we received was soggy rice. Couldn't really find any fish. Put us off Paella for life!! To top it off this cast us 50 euros. Could have made this at home for a pound! This is my first ever negative review on Tripadvisor. Don't come here!!
name: Restaurante Bar La Bouganvilla

text: Went here twice on our 7 day holiday. And it wasn't just because of the food it was because of the lovely service and family atmosphere in the restaurant where you would get involved with other conversations amongst the owners, and other family's. It only offers outside seating but it sheltered and as it's in Spain, is very rarely a problem. Would definitely recommend if you're in the area.
name: The Town Frier

text: We pre booked a table for 13 for our arrival in puerto banus on a hen weekend - everything was perfect. The table was laid out beautifully with balloons and gold confetti and the staff were so friendly and welcoming. The view of the beach js one of the best in the port. All our food was lovely and came our on time. We will definitely come back! Thanks for getting out hen weekend off to such a great start!
name: Celebrities Gold Restaurant Pizzeria

text: We must be grateful to Malaga City Council for allowing this Escuela de Hosteleria to continue teaching the arts of cooking and food service. The restaurant is set in magnificent gardens and a glass of cava on the terrace is a must. Then sit back and enjoy the most delicious foods and wine. This is an experience not to be missed and to be repeated as often as possible and quite frankly at a very reasonable price. Even if there was an equivalent in London, it would be at five times the price.
name: La Consula

text: It was the first day of our holiday, we were tired from the journey and the long day so stopped here as it was the first restaurant along the promenade. The title says it all really, no complaints about the quality or quantity of the food or the value for money, but the service was average at best. There are so many restaurants along here that, unfortunately, average is not really good enough and so we did not return.
name: The Water Front

text: We stopped here on our way back to the airport, the food was very nice and you got a whole round of drinks free once you had bought one round, there are many restaurants in the port and they are all very expensive for what you get, good location right next to the sea, I guess this is what you pay for, the staff were very pleasent.
name: Gaucho Grill Benalmadena

text: Went there with party of 8. We had to book the day before. Food was fantastic. Especially the specials. Black pasta and fish were superb. Wine was excellent. Staff superb. Very frienfly and attentive but not over powering. Dining area inside has aircon and outside is sheltered from any breeze by a very smart set of glass screen. A must visit place. Not the cheapest meal we had but you get what you pay for.
name: San Rocco

text: This is tucked away in a side street, the clientele mainly Spanish, so some basic Spanish maybe required. There are some meat dishes on the menu but this is not a place to go to eat meat. Freshly caught fish is displayed at the entrance which you can choose from, also there are various delicious freshly made salads. Very reasonable prices.
name: Casa Rafael Papa Erig

text: They are one busy pizza and pasta restaurant! It's always jammed packed with people any time of the day. We love their deliciously thin pizza vs the "sexy pasta" they are known for. We did try a few of their pasta over the course of a few visits but we think the true star of the place is their pizza. The owner or manager of the place is quite a charming guy with a great sense of humor. This casual Puerto Banus pizza heaven for us is always a must when we're in town!
name: La Pappardella

text: The food is absolutely amazing and having had many trips to India and someone who eats Indian food regularly in the UK this restaurants food is truly amazing!!! The staff are always so friendly and the food always amazing! I visit every week when I am in Chiclana. If you like Indian you will love it, if you've never tried it you will love it. Well done Taj Mahal and staff 10/10!!!
name: Taj Mahal Chiclana Spain

text: I thought I would give this place another try after and awful experience last year just to give them the benefit of the doubt. What a mistake that was!! The service was just as bad this year. We left last year after waiting half an hour for a drink and still not getting it and this year we placed an order for four drinks and a bottle of water only and they couldn't manage to get that right first time either. The chef came out a one point arguing with a customer about what she ordered! I will definitely not be giving this a third chance which is a pity because it is in the beautiful church square in the centre of Competa.
name: Perico

text: My son and I stopped by chance for lunch on Tuesday and shared tapas dishes. The food was good and the service was excellent. Despite the many restaurants available we chose to return for an evening meal on Thursday and were served once again by Manuela who gave helpful and delicious recommendations. We had eaten the previous evening at a very popular and highly rated restaurant and, for us, Mosaic was a much more enjoyable experience.
name: Restaurante Mosaico

text: Just visited this restaurant & had a wonderful meal. Huge choice of menu but I am a very fussy eater and requested modifications to the wild mushroom pasta (no cream or salt). The most delicious mushroom linguine was served to me....exactly as ordered! My starter of bruschetta classico was also delicious. Husband ordered ham & mushroom pizza which he said was the best he has eaten in a long time. Wine menu was extensive & we were delighted with the Ribera Del Douro which waitress recommended. We will definitely return here before the end of our holiday. Thank you to the waitress & chef for listening to our requests. Also, to finish, we enjoyed limoncellos on the house. Do come here & enjoy fantastic evening!
name: Bella Roma

text: This looks like an Italian restaurant with a small board advertising the Paella. We got in and actually ordered one along with some garlic bread with cheese. We asked him to make the Paella spicy and what came out was something that we had not eaten in a long long time. One of the best Paella's that we have eaten so far. Simply amazing !
name: Pasta Fresca Restaurante

text: Called in for lunch 5 tapas and 2 beers only 10 Euro. All freshly cooked, you could select anything off tapas menu. Great value. Drinks very reasonable. Also enjoyed the best cocktails we've had all week for only 4.50 Euro. Had dessert too panna cotta, beautiful. This place deserves to do well. Staff are friendly, helpful and proud of their establishment. Pity it's our last day. Will be back in December. Thank you.
name: 274 Co

text: Went here for dinner one night as we were wandering the streets looking for somewhere to eat. Didn't realise it was Chinese at first but were seated quickly on the terrace, given prawn crackers while we decided on our food choices and drinks order was taken straight away. The food was excellent and the service was very quick. Good value for money meant a large tip. Would recommend and visit again.
name: Restaurant Asiatico Yuan

text: We were thrown off at first because the restaurant was outside of Ronda and in a residential area, but We LOVED this family restaurant. The food was DELICIOUS, but what made it one of our favorite restaurants on our trip was the warmth of the father and son who spent time talking to us. It is a special experience for sure! Worth the short trip outside of Ronda.
name: Tropicana

text: I really enjoyed my experience here. The food was delicious and very well prepared. I'd read that the dishes weren't very big so we ordered a lot (4 between us). It was too much food and when we couldn't eat the soup the restaurant refused to let us pay, even though we tried to insist. Excellent service, wonderful food. Will definitely go back.
name: Moon

text: Go here for lunchtime menu of half price pizzas.5-5.50 euros for huge freshly baked pizzas sat in great seating area right beside the ocean.This offer not available in August but otherwise all year round.Salads good too if a little pricey. Yes,the service can be a little tardy but no more than other places on the Playa at busy times of the year.
name: Imperial Playa

text: I live 50 meters from this restaurant and love it. I try to go alone. When my wife is away. It is a place for adults, full of charming, talkative people eating great pig, lamb, beef, cooked on the grill, large glasses of red wine, superb baked potatoes stuffed with sour cream, Jamon to start, a small plate of cheese to finish. In the summer it is sweet relief from the chiringuitos, in winter, warm, cosy, a place I don't want to leave. May it continue long after I am gone.
name: El Botijo Malaga

text: La Paella Sevilla - owned and run by a Valencian family, is home to Seville's most reliable paella. Their menu is tiny, with only six choices, but that guarantees that they will be prepared to perfection. There were no vegan or vegetarian options, only seafood, and meat. You can add a sauce made of egg, olive, and garlic for 50p extra. You will also find fideuà (noodles instead of rice). After ordering they will heat it up in a microwave. I have tried paella de marisco (seafood), which was salty for my taste with some undercooked rice. I am not a food critic and maybe my taste bud is not made for this. Service was good, and for the price of just 3.5 Euros for a small seafood takeaway paella, you cannot expect more. I just wanted to taste it that is it - the small portion will be not enough for one person.
name: La Paella Sevilla

text: Need I say more? Really? If you are thinking about your favorite pasta dish, dun. Except for lasagne, the creations are unique. I'd never thought pasta could be this interesting. Simple in style and ingredients, yet amazingly wonderful. Love the sacchettini, ravioli w pumkin. The tiramisu is the best I've ever had. Simple, intense flavours, no gimmicks. High quality chocolate powder dusted over it. Great selection of wines. Personable service, homey cosy little place. Portions are a little too healthy for me. But hey! that leaves space for desserts and more wines.
name: La Dolce Vita

text: Nowhere near Nobu London or NYC standards, except for the price. We dined there Aug 22. Seems to cater to the hotel guests, rather than sushi lovers. Many kids and people ordering salads. Beautiful setting if you're on the terrace. Inside tables have too much noise. Friendly but inattentive service. Our sushi pieces had so much wasabi inside, that it overpowered and was hard to distinguish the type of fish. Rolls offered were nothing special. We have had better Black Cod and Tiger shrimp tempura in various sushi restaurants in Spain. Very disappointing. Nobu will lose its valuable brand name if it franchises to places like this.
name: Nobu Restaurant Lounge Marbella

text: We were looking through trip advisor for recommendations of a good local tapas restaurant, and Captains stood out. After a lovely welcome and a lovely cold cerveza, we were feeling confident but sadly the food was not able to maintain the level expected. There was nothing bad, but the menu seems a little confused and not enough choice with the tapas. With a little bit of TLC and menu adaptation this could be a gem.
name: Captains Mojacar International Tapas Restaurant

text: Been here every time we visit Marbs, the most welcoming , I don't like to call her a waitress , she's much more than that, owners wife tbh. She's brilliant, bubbly and attentive, superb brekkie , everything cooked as we like it. Coffee to die for , superb location, overlooking the sea. Also had early evening drinks there, great red vino , reasonably priced. Can't reiterate how the owners wife could teach so many others about customer orientation , brilliant.
name: Blue Palm

text: A restaurant shows it's true colors on the day after Christmas, and La Marea did a very good job. They were able to get us a table despite how late it was during the afternoon meal and our service was splendid. No need to wait for ANYTHING throughout the entire meal. We had ensaladilla as our appetizer and it was delicious. I would wager that it is the best I've had in quite some time. The owner came out to meet us and put together a nice selection of seafood platters for us to try. We had miniature crab claws, mussels, and a nice fried fish surtido. Drinks were constantly being refilled and everything was delightful. Very highly recommended for your sea side if you are craving fresh fish or crustations.
name: La Marea de Marcos Restaurante Marisqueria

text: We called in without a reservation late afternoon. Had a table inside and were attended to immediately. Large selection of pastas and pizzas, with every kind of pasta and extras you can think of. The lasagne el forno was very tasty and well presented, the only criticism was the portion size, it was on the small side and didn't come with anything, the tiramisu made up for it and was substantial and gorgeous. Nice atmosphere and great to see the open kitchen and the chefs at work.
name: Ginos Fuengirola

text: Chose this restaurant at the last minute and got chicken Tandoori to start. Chicken was a bit dry and tough and the main was bland. My partner got the Spinach dish wish tasted of mulched Spinach and yoghurt. Pretty disappointing so this is only my opinion but wish I had been advised as I would have given it a miss.
name: Harry s Restro

text: Avoid at all costs. Food was like eating oily slop. Asked for extra spicy curry and it tasted of absolutely nothing. Food was that bad that myself and my partner could not eat it. I tried to tell the waitress who pretended she didnt understand what I was saying. Paid the bill (which was still full price even after complaining and eating nothing) and walked down the road to another restaurant for a pizza.
name: Palacio Chino

text: We were a group of 4 and had been recommended this restaurant. The food was of a very high standard and all our dishes were excuse. We had tried to just call in the night before, but they were fully booked so we are glad we made a reservation. The service was also of a very high standard. Highly recommended...
name: Torres y Garcia

text: El Botijo started in Malaga, owned by Gaby and Jose from Haro, the main Rioja town in Northern Spain. The Malaga restaurant is always full of locals (I have never seen a tourist in there) due to the excellence of their meat, and lamb in particular. The appetizers and the main courses are simple presentations. For example, grilled asparagus is exactly that with sea salt and virgin olive oil. What they lack in flourishes they make up for in the quality of the ingredients and excellent of the cooking. There is a decent wine list of about 35 drinkables rather than an extensive selection. They opened a second restaurant just off the Carihuela in Torremolinos where Jose presides. The decor in very Spanish looking with dark woods, mounted animal skulls and paintings on the wall. The skulls are real and remainders from Jose's hunting trips. Dinner for 2 approximately 80 Euros including a 20 Euro wine (There are many below and some above).
name: El Botijo Malaga

text: Charolais has been here many years and caters more to local people who know where to eat in the town centre. Originaly more of a Bodega that served quality food with an excellent wine list which from a mark up point of view is very fairly priced. The restaurant now has 3 sections, a fabulous modern tapas area, a covered terrace section which is great for smokers and the original central bodega. As with Los Manueles the meat is sourced from local farms and the owner is very passionate about everything he serves. If you are a cheese fan he serves a superb Manchego as a tapas of which he is very proud. This is more of a quality restaurant rather than a quick meal during a family holiday. A couple of the waiters do speak some English so you will manage to communicate what you want!! Fuengirola now seems to have some good options for quality food rather than just quick meals, this is certainly one of them.
name: Bodega Restaurante Charolais

text: What a gem! Off the tourist trap circuit despite having a great location on the prettiest plaza in Cadiz. Almost always busy, with a great selection of wines on hand. We never ate on the restaurant side - always seemed to miss time this - but the food looks great. I might call it casual-gourmet-spanish. The attached store has the best bocadillos in town and beyond, and a huge selection of conservas, wines, etc. The staff seems to work tirelessly every single day, all hours that they are open, and are very helpful and efficient (you probably won't be bantering with them much as they are busy!).
name: El Chicuco

text: We booked a table for 4 people Sunday Lunchtime. We arrived slightly early, but no table had been reserved for us. Eventually we were shown to a table and asked if we wanted drinks and given the menu. We ordered starters which took ages to arrive but were really nice. After waiting an hour and others around had been served with main courses we asked about ours and was told they were coming.... salmon in paper arrived in tin foil and stone cold, two tenderloin steaks one rare the other well done arrived both medium with dried up vegetables and the Argentine steak on a stone was all fat and gristle. I've seen better stewing steak. Two people asked for jacket potato but were served chips. The service was nil, one of us had to go to the bar and ask for coffee and the bill. When we complained the waiter didn't understand although two people at the table spoke fluent Spanish. Never again.
name: Safari Lounge

text: We visited this venue on our WeLoveMalaga tapas tour with Victor last Friday. I guess you'd describe it as a modern wine cellar which also serves tapas. Quite unusual and different from the other bars and restaurant's we'd visited. It really suited our taste. The tapas was more modern, and the wine was delicious. We were well looked after by our host Julian. We liked it so much, we returned the following lunchtime and talked to Julian about shipping some wine home. We've tried to ship wine in many different countries, and sometimes it proves very difficult to achieve. Not so at Los Patios de Beatas ! A great tasting, an easy transaction, and a very reasonable price. Plus we really enjoyed the food. Surprised this place hasn't got a higher rating on TA, but well worth a visit if you like your wine.
name: Los Patios de Beatas

text: Visiting the Jewish Museum in Seville the young guide there told us that the old Jewish bath house was now the San Marco Restaurant. We decided to go that evening . The ground floor of this indoor / outdoor establishment was indeed a bath house , and from the wall and arches , back to Moorish times . The food offering is excellent as was our service , and all accompanied by a sold Spanish guitar player . We opted to share the degustation/ tapas menu with my wife adding an anchovie pasta dish . All was delicious. Chasing history and culture we were rewarded with a gastronomic delight .
name: San Marco Barrio Santa Cruz

text: Great seafood, excellent service, right on the beach. Followed the server's recommendations and had a whole fresh fish, which tasted very fresh. Also followed the server's recommendations on an appetizer and the wine and was not disappointed. We also ordered a tuna dish. which was good, but not great. I think 'rare' to us is a little different than 'rare' here, which I'm not going to fault them for. The perfect location to see the sunset, which was stunning.
name: La Ola Restaurant Lounge Bar

text: After visiting the Alcazar we stumbled upon this little gem, since we have been in Spain for days now we wanted to try a different cuisine so that's why we were happy to walk into this Lebanese place. The manager is extremely friendly and attentive, and even mentioned we were ordering too much food (which was of course appreciated). The food was delicious - the labaneh and kebe chamieh specially- as was the rest of the dishes ordered, and the baklava and tea as well. Would absolutely recommend, service was fast and prices reasonable.
name: El Rincon De Beirut

text: We have been here many times and it's because it's a place where you can dress up and eat inside or relax outside under the stars. We sat in the window inside as it wasn't a warm evening but we had a heater close by and it wasn't very busy so we had full attention by the staff, sadly the young girl serving us was a little too eager to serve that I had to ask her to wait before bringing main course or we would have been finished in an hour! We shared a starter and I had the stir fry which was fabulous however very pricey for a simple dish. We decided to sit in their lounge area afterwards for a digestive and suddenly there was no staff! Waited a long time but it was nice chatting and sitting comfortably. The decor is amazing and you feel like you are in a lodge in Africa which I love best about this place.
name: Trocadero Arena

text: We always visit San Rocco when we are in Roquetas - the food is always excellent quality. Yes you can get cheaper elsewhere, but you do get what you pay for! The decor and service is lovely .Leave room for tiramisu which I prefer to the cheesecake ( one day I might go and just have two sweets then I can have both!).
name: San Rocco

text: What a mistake choosing this restaurant. The quality of the food did not live up to the prices. The service was even worse, the waiters paid no attention to our table of 6 at all. Our main meals arrived before the starters had been finished or plates cleared away. Meals were given without cutlery to eat it with. The only lobster in the lobster paella was the shell. The advacado and prawn starter contained very few small prawns. No offer of vegetables with the fish dishes. Hard dry bread for which we were charged €1 each. Would not recommend there are far more better restaurants to visit. We did not leave a tip as we usually would have done, in comparison the day before we left a €50 tip in another restaurant to acknowledge how good it was.
name: Casa Juan Los Mellizos

text: Dined here on our first night and was not disappointed. Sat on the balcony and it was fairly busy but not rammed. The pate, bread and nibbles were very good. The service is efficient and prompt. They were friendly enough without being in your face. If you want a friend go somewhere else. The lamb was very very good and fell off the bone. Huge portions and a very good price.
name: Rufino

text: I have been to Noviembre several times, cause I really like the valuable food. That's the only reason why I went there that often. The service is just horrible. The waitors/waitresses need like 15 minutes at least to overcome that they need to serve you at all. Then, many times a lot of the ingredients were already gone (which of course is not their fault), but they act like they don't care at all about what you want with for instance making suggestions for other food. They are very inconsiderate and sometimes even rude!!!!
name: Noviembre

text: This was my first visit and right from the start I was really impressed. The place has a lovely easy, fun relaxed feel to it. The service staff were lovely. The menu has some lovely imaginative options - their wok vegetables dishes looked wonderful coming out of the kitchen - so that is what I opted for. I opted to add fish and prawns to mine. When it arrived the presentation was wonderful and it smelled great too. The only problem was- they forgot to add my prawns and fish! But you can tell the quality of a restaurant by how they deal with mistakes - and these guys get 10 out of 10 for how they sorted this out. They were so apologetic and the chef came out to say sorry too. In no time at all I had exactly what I ordered and it was well worth the wait.
name: Safari Lounge

text: Tucked away in the sprawling hills of Mojacer Playa lies this brilliant restaurant, with amazing views from the covered outside terrace overlooking a swimming pool. Open 6 days a week(closed Mondays) we visited with a party of 9 and all chose the menu del dia charged at €10 for 3 courses with multiple choices on each course, all cooked to perfection by the proprietor/chef Shea, who could not do enough for our party. All in all a wonderful meal with charming service and one certainly not to be missed if in the area. Highly recommended.
name: Restaurante La Parata

text: Its located in the quietest part of the street, with attentive and knowledgeable waiter service, where you can taste classic Italian dishes, cooked by an Italian. The carbonara pasta, prepared with egg yolk and bacon, some eggplants with cheese or the pizza itself attest to how these typical Italian dishes should be prepared. I the table next to us there was a group that had asked for a special risotto (you have to ask for it in advance) saying that it was spectacular. Desserts, in this case, a homemade ice cream, was also delicious.
name: Tutto Bene Trattoria By Little Italy

text: Tis is one of the best places to eat in Fuengirola.Just on the edge of Plaza Chinorros it is head and shoulders above the others in the square. Unusual tapas, very decent sized portions and reasonably priced decent wine. Try anything with langoustines and the plantain with avocado is great. The staff are pleasant and helpful but over the past couple of years have managed on two occasions to add a bottle of wine instead of a glass to my bill. No problem getting it removed from the bill, but a bit annoying. Great place to spend a couple of hours.
name: Tatin Ultramarinos Restaurante

text: I have eaten in Casanis many times this year. Both for business and for pleasure. The food is exquisite and the service impeccable. The ambiance inside which is an old building right in the centre of old town Marbella is devine and the hustle and bustle when seated outside allows you to watch the world go by, as well as watch the staff cook your meal in the kitchen. (Go to see what I mean). Both provide a perfect holiday photo opportunity. The consistently good food and cocktails bring me back regularly and the staff are extremely professional, polite and very charming. I for sure highly recommend Casanis as a fine dining experience. Enjoy.
name: Casanis Bistrot Restaurant

text: we were looking for a takeaway Indian and found this one did takeaway,it was excellent as my wife is vegetarian and gluten intolerant and my daughter likes fish balti ,they were most helpful and accommodating, i had garlic naan excellent,chicken pakora,chicken shaslik,my wife vegetable korma,and rice,very reasonably priced for 3 and was still warm after a ten minute drive back to apartment.
name: Masala Korma

text: A disappointing evening at this restaurant - after 75 minutes all we had had to eat was a bowl of tomatoes and asparagus, the chips then arrived and eventually the octopus but this was luke warm (it was taken away to be warmed up but obviously in a microwave and was still only warm) and by now the chips were cold. Still no sign of the other tapas of tuna and anchovies! We asked where the rest of the food was and decided we would leave. We offered to pay but the restaurant said no they would not charge us and apologised which was very good of them but the evening had been ruined.
name: Lobito de Mar Marbella

text: This was our third visit to this restaurant. Our 2nd visit in September 2012 was disappointing because despite talking to the maitre'd, at length, about our dislike of bloody steaks, when they arrived they were rare regardless of us ordering medium to well done. We sent steaks back and when they returned they were still very bloody. What a difference on this visit. We ordered food and crossed our fingers. The Steaks were cooked to perfection and so delicious probably one of the best we have had. Service is friendly. The menu is not big on vegetables so steer clear if any of your party is vegetarian. I will consider oing again.
name: La Cabana Bar Grill
